articleTitle: A capacity expansion planning model integrating hybrid PV-storage stations with grid export constraints
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper evaluates the integration of tightly coupled photovoltaic-plus-storage stations subject to export constraints in power systems experiencing high renewable energy sources (RES) penetration levels. The power output limitations imposed on the hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and storage installations stem from the restricted available electrical space of the system to accommodate new RES capacity. A suitably developed capacity expansion planning model optimizing the energy mix of the Greek power system for a 90% RES penetration target is developed to perform the study. Analysis considers the climate conditions of 35 historical years to avoid skewing the obtained results due to the peculiarities of a single climatic year. Simulation results show that in the absence of power output limitations for PV-storage stations, around 31 GW of RES units are required, occupying equivalent electrical space and necessitating upgrades to the existing grid. Conversely, when export constraints are applied to hybrid stations, the required electrical space to accommodate renewables is reduced by ~17%, with the export limit of the PV-storage configurations being as low as 30%. An additional annual system cost reduction of 5.2% is also obtained compared with a baseline case where PVs and storages cannot be effectively coupled within the algorithm.

articleTitle: Modelling of faults in HVDC systems in the outage calculation for congestion management
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of the European transmission grid with HVDC systems, the handling of faults in the HVDC system is increasingly coming into focus. For some years, there has been a de velopment from point-to-point (P2P) connections to multi-terminal HVDC systems (MTDC systems). A fault on an HVDC line can result in a loss of transport capacity whereas converter faults can lead to a situation where no feed-in or feed-out is possible at the connected grid node. If the power from the HVDC system is fed into the AC grid, congestion can occur there. Due to the increased integration of HVDC systems into the European transmission grid, the outages of HVDC converters and HVDC lines must be consi dered in future outage calculations. As the converters are actively controllable components, the effect of the loss of the controller within the converter must al so be taken into account. The aim of the work is therefore to propose a model to simulate outa ges in HVDC systems and their effect on the AC grid. Exemplary results on a modified IEEE 118 node network show that the (n-1) outage of a bipole converter leads to a load flow shift in the AC. The system balance of the HVDC system and the effects of the c ontrol strategies are taken into account. The result of the outage calculation can be used as input for a subsequent congestion management simulation.

articleTitle: Security-constrained optimization framework for integrated active and reactive power optimization of transmission grid operation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: As the energy transition and decarbonization require higher line utilization and optimization of the transmission grid, the challenges for transmission grid operation are increasing. Optimization problems to support decision-making in current-related congestion management or voltage control typically focus either on the optimization of active power-related degrees of freedom or on the optimization of reactive power-related degrees of freedom. In order to address the interactions arising in the context of increasing line utilization and more volatile power flows in the future, this paper presents an approach for an integrated optimization of current- and voltage-related congestions, considering interdependencies. In this paper, the integrated optimization is validated on a test grid derived from the IEEE 118 bus network and compared with a sequential run of a separate active power optimization and a subsequent reactive power optimization. The exemplary results show that, the integrated optimization will potentially identify more efficient and secure measures compared to the separate sequential optimization.

articleTitle: Optimizing the operation of energy storage systems using artificial intelligence for economic performance and energy transition
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The utilization of energy storage systems (ESS) and the expansion of their installed capacity are crucial steps towards achieving energy neutrality goals. These systems, often integrated with photovoltaic installations, represent an intermediate stage that introduces new challenges for distribution management and financial burdens for consumers and society. To maximize the benefits of ESS, it is necessary to design an optimization system that considers the battery lifecycle, installed capacity, a nd economic benefits. A key objective is the determination and reduction of the per-unit usage cost of these systems, which represents a significant innovation of this work. This paper proposes an optimization model that incorporates factors such as energy pricing, charging/discharging efficiency, battery lifespan, and renewable energy forecasts. The model leverages artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, for data analysis and decision-making based on historical data and patterns. This solution is designed to address the needs of both residential and industrial clients, further expanding its applicability. This approach optimizes the economic performance of ESS, minimizes energy transition costs, and fosters favorable conditions for a successful transition.

articleTitle: Smart meter-based outage detection and fault location in a microgrid in Gaidouromantra, Greece
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In the existing literature, Digital relay-based protection schemes are proposed for microgrids (MGs). Digital relays are expensive and uneconomical for practical microgrids. However, in most MGs, smart meters (SMs) with communication facilities are available at the consumer end for energy measurements. These SMs can measure the electrical quantities and communicate the measurements to the local server. This paper demonstrates that SMs can also be used for outage detection and fault location in practical MGs. Gaidouromantra MG is one such MG in Kythnos island, Greece, with SMs and communication facilities. This paper proposes two algorithms to detect outages and fault locations. The first algorithm is a voltage-based algorithm which assumes that SM communication is intact. The second algorithm extends the first. It uses current measurements along with voltage measurements to tackle the problem of SM communication disconnection after the fault. The algorithms use measurements from the SMs to detect the outage in the feeder and locate the fault with the guidance of the MG's topology. Additionally, the extended algorithm can be used to indicate SM communication failure and no-load/disconnection status of houses on the island, if any occur. The algorithms are validated using the Gaidouromantra MG model on Simulink and hardware-in-loop simulations of the Gaidouromantra MG. The proposed algorithms can generally be applied to MGs with radial structures consisting of a single grid-forming inverter and multiple grid-following inverters, as in Gaidouromantra.

articleTitle: Evaluating microgrid controllers using an advanced hardware-in-the-loop testing chain integrated with digital twin technology
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Digital twin technology, leveraging sensor data to replicate physical systems, offers a potent means to validate equipment dynamics and control strategies. This paper presents an advanced Hardware-in-the-Loop setup coupled with a Real-Time Digital Twin for evaluating the performance of the ecoMG tool—an Energy Management System tailored for microgrids and small off-grid systems. Demonstrating its effectiveness, the digital twin of Gaidouro- mantra MG is utilized with real-time data from the field. The results demonstrate that the proposed setup, despite its complexity, enables the thorough evaluation of the tool as part of the overall system.

articleTitle: Green energy and storage integration - the case study of Ikaria
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Recently there is a global effort to reduce carbon dioxide emissions and modernize the electric power systems (EPS) in order to provide green and stable energy to consumers, while also taking cost minimization into account. To achieve this, production from Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in tandem with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) is being proposed and integrated to EPS around the world. However, the dispersed and intermittent nature of RES, the differing ESS technologies, the variety of landscapes on a local level and the fact that those solutions must be incorporated into the existing infrastructures, impose the need for further studying the optimal implementation of those new technologies without power disruptions, while ensuring grid stability through the provision of ancillary services. The Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) is responsible for the wider Greek distribution network, as well as the Non- Interconnected Islands (NIIs). The NIIs in particular can be considered excellent test beds for new technologies and innovative solutions, since they are insular microgrids and therefore, can provide immediate feedback on implemented changes. This paper will focus on the island of Ikaria; mainly on the effort of modernizing the grid management as well as the possibility of expanding upon the lessons learned to the rest of the Greek electricity grid.

articleTitle: Optimal operation and analysis of a district heating supplier's portfolio: the Swedish case
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper develops a mixed integer linear program (MILP) for optimal operation modelling and analysis of a district heating supplier’s portfolio. The model aims to meet the heat demand with the lowest possible dispatch cost, while maximizing the profit from electricity trading in competitive day-ahead (DA) and manual frequency restorations reserves (mFRR) regulation markets. The proposed price driven MILP model is applied on a real system of a Swedish district heating (DH) company, namely Tekniska verken i Link¨oping AB (TvAB), to analyse the operation of TvAB’s portfolio and the resulting participation in DA and mFRR markets. It is seen that an optimal operation of the portfolio while trading in the DA market alone results in a profit of about 156 MSEK, while also considering participation in mFRR markets in addition to DA increases the profit by another 2.75 MSEK.

articleTitle: Lightning impulse flashover modelling of a typical MV porcelain insulator using ATP-EMTP: application to a MV overhead distribution line
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Flashover prediction of medium voltage overhead line insulators is of great importance in insulation coordination studies . In electromagnetic transient simulations insulator flashover is modelled using experimentally obtained flashover volt-time curves, or the integration method with parameters appropriately adjusted based on experimental flashover results. However, these modelling approaches, being specifically related to the reference experimental results, cannot be easily generalised to apply to the great variety of utilized distribution line insulators, differing in geometry and material, as well as to the variability in the waveshape and polarity of the lightning surge overvoltages. In this study a modelling approach for lightning impulse flashover of typical MV overhead line insulators is introduced, based on the CIGRE leader progression model however with its model parameters appropriately adjusted. An excellent agreement between experimental and modelling flashover results has been achieved by expressing model parameters as a function of the average steepness of the applied voltage at leader inception. The developed model is implemented in ATP-EMTP environment to evaluate insulation flashover of an overhead line of the Hellenic distribution system due to direct positive lightning strikes. The main advantage of developed leader progression model is its ability to accurately describe the dynamics of discharge growth over insulators, starting from leader inception up to flashover.

articleTitle: Coordinated control of load tap changers and distributed energy resources for voltage regulation in active distribution systems
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a voltage control method for active distribution systems based on the coordinated operation of on-load-tap-changers (OLTCs) and distributed energy resources (DERs). Primarily, DERs are assigned to control local voltage when overvoltage/undervoltage conditions appear in the system. DER control actions are initiated based on predetermined local voltage criteria and they result in properly changing the active and/or reactive power output of DERs. In case DER control is not adequate to keep voltages within the acceptable operation limits, the LTCs of the MV/LV power transformers are properly controlled to restore local voltages. As a tertiary measure, the LTC of the main substation power transformer regulates the voltage to keep network voltages within permissible limits. Coordination between local voltage control actions is guaranteed with appropriate selection of thresholds. Several scenarios considering hourly time-varying load demand and variable electricity production from DERs are simulated. The proposed voltage control method is tested against several scenarios. Simulation results show that the proposed method efficiently controls voltage in active distribution systems.

articleTitle: Solar energy solution for small autonomous islands
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Solar energy is an inexhaustible and clean energy resource. Greek islands possess high solar energy potential, but they still cover their electric energy needs mainly using thermal power stations or interconnections with sub-marine cables with larger islands. This situation results in low-quality energy needs fulfilment with high electricity generation cost and degradation of the environment mainly due to the CO2 emissions. The significant exploitation of the available solar potential is practically limited by the dynamic stability of local weak electrical networks. For this purpose, the introduction of energy storage and demand side management is a challenging option. Thus, to bypass the above-mentioned constraints and to secure a more sustainable electricity supply status, the concept of combining photovoltaic (PV) power stations and energy storage systems comprises a promising solution for small-scaled autonomous electrical networks. This paper presents a complete methodology able to define the optimum size of an autonomous power electrical generation system with maximum solar energy penetration, calculating the required dimensions of the photovoltaic installation combined with the necessary capacity of the storage system. Ideally, zer o energy production from the thermal power system is the target, but other factors, such us high initial investment cost and maximum system reliability should be also taken into account. In this context, the main idea of the current work is to provide a concise methodology, based on real world data, able to determine an optimal electrification solution of small non-interconnected islands, based on solar energy exploitation and energy storage utilization, in order to minimize the electricity generation cost and the corresponding greenhouse emissions supporting also the energy supply security of the local community.

articleTitle: Traction control and antilock braking control performance analysis in distributed drive electric vehicle on split ramps
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The drivability of split ramps is an essential dynamic performance of electric vehicles (EVs). Nevertheless, the existing traction control system (TCS) demands additional braking assistance for optimal driving control. This work proposes a novel TCS for distributed drive electric vehicles (DDEV) to improve traction and reduce energy demand. This work presents a slope-seeking traction force allocation approach assisted by an anti-lock braking system (ABS) for practical driving on the uphill and downhill split ramp surface. A genetic algorithm is used to determine the optimum values of the traction force at various road-grade angles. Simulated results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed TCS in driving and braking conditions. The proposed TCS has the potential to improve the pass ability, reduce the power requirement, and reduce the system complexity and cost.

articleTitle: Grid topology classification heuristic using the time coordination in adaptive protection systems
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an alternative approach to classifying grid topologies in adaptive protection systems, focusing on time coordination rather than traditional clustering methods. By grouping grid topologies based on main and backup relay pairs, our method ensures that similar protection requirements are met across different grid topologies. Our comprehensive simulations reveal that the selection of the initial solution significantly impacts the formation of grid topology classes and the resulting time-dial settings in the Setting Groups. These findings emphasize the importance of multiple heuristic runs to achieve robust Setting Groups determination and reliable protection performance.

articleTitle: Mapping grid impedance effect by aggregated loads in LV grids
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: With converters taking an increasing part in the grid, the impact of supraharmonic disturbances increases. The impact of these disturbances is, to a large extent, dependant on the grid impedance at the place and frequency of the disturbance. The grid impedance, in turn, is dependent on both the grid topology and the surrounding loads. This paper shows that the impedance of an aggregated distant load impacts the grid impedance in distinct ways for different frequencies. Additionally, the paper shows that the length of the cables closest to the measurement site have a larger impact on the maximum possible impedance than the cables closer to the variable load.

articleTitle: A method for monitoring slow electromechanical oscillations in multi-area electrical power systems: the case of four areas IEEE 39 bus power system
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper illustrates an earlier introduced method for systematic monitoring and control of slow electro-mechanical oscillations in electric power systems. The emphasis is on generalizing the two-area system concepts to a general multi-area power system. The method illustrates a transformed state space which explicitly models tie-line flow power dynamics between areas of interest (groups of interconnected equipment) and the rest of the system. Given parameters of an electric power grid, these tie-line power flow oscillations are expressed in terms of load and generation power deviations from given equilibrium, both controlled and uncontrolled. This new model sets the basis for identifying root causes of slow inter-area oscillations, needed to define the most important measurements and placement/enhancement of controllers for reducing these interactions. Notably, both conventional model and the transformed state space model have the same eigenvalues. The proposed approach does not require eigenmode calculations, and therefore lends itself to practical use of Phasor Measurmeent Units (PMUs). It is then shown how each area can monitor, compute and control inter-area oscillations either in an entirely decentralized way, much the same way as today’s Automatic Generation Control (AGC) is carried out, or in a cooperative efficient way by jointly controlling inter-area fluctuations.

articleTitle: A state estimator using synchronized phasor measurements for power systems containing VSC-HVDC links with converter losses
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This article focuses on enhancing the formulation and implementation of state estimator (SE) using phasor measurements units (PMU) for transmission systems including voltage source converter (VSC) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) links. An equality constrained SE considering synchronized phasor measurements for hybrid power systems is proposed, where AC/DC power losses in the VSC station are taken into consideration. The associated measurement model encompasses both AC and DC measurements. For the AC network, PMU devices supply with synchronized voltage and current phasor measurements the SE. DC measurements are acquired from the DC side of the VSC stations and are assumed to be sampled at the same rate as the synchronized phasor measurements. Zero injections and AC/DC coupling equations are modeled as equality constraints. The effectiveness and estimation accuracy of the proposed algorithm are demonstrated on complex AC/HVDC test systems.

articleTitle: Critical comparison of the measurement accuracy of DGA techniques for the timely detection of emerging faults
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In the context of modern energy engineering, power transformers constitute one of the most critical parts, as they ensure the efficient conversion and distribution of electrical energy throughout the power grid. The reliability of transformers , is fundamental for the safe and continuous operation of the network, and the timely detection and diagnosis of potential faults is essential. This paper focuses on the Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) method, as a primary tool for analyzing and detecting emerging faults in transformers. Specifically, DGA techniques are based on the principle that various faults within the transformer lead to the production of specific gases, which are dissolved in the oil used for insulation and cooling of the u nit. Analyzing the composition and concentration of these gases can provide valuable information about the nature and severity of the faults. Additionally, in this paper an analysis and comparison is conducted between the offline DGA monitoring and online DGA monitoring used for analyzing transformer gases, focusing on the accuracy of each technique.

articleTitle: Optimization of a multi-energy system with the application of info-gap approach in different risk attitudes
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: With increasing concerns about climate change and the need for cleaner energy sources, the integration of different energy resources and sectors is a key driver in transitioning towards more sustainable and flexible future multi-energy systems. Their integration not only enables whole power system cost-efficiency, flexibility and resiliency but also empowers consumers to optimize energy consumption, encouraging a more flexible and customer-centric energy landscape. To enhance the economic performance of distributed energy systems, this paper focuses on studying a multi-energy system with the integration of electricity, gas and heating/cooling sectors. This research aims to address demand uncertainty, a critical parameter influencing economic feasibility. To achieve this, the information-gap decision method is adopted, enabling effective management and mitigation of potential risks associated with volatile electrical and thermal demands. This approach seeks to ensure the optimal economic performance of the multi-energy system under varying market conditions for decision-makers with various risk attitudes. The robustness of decisions against worst-case scenarios is evaluated using a robustness model, analyzing various risk levels to provide a comprehensive view for decision-makers. On the other side, an opportunity function is utilized to address the risk-seeker point of view. As part of this optimization approach, we thoroughly analyze the role of electrical energy storage as a buffer to facilitate efficient energy utilization in the studied multi-energy system. This integration aims to optimize energy supply and demand, analyzing the economic benefits of a multi-energy system when considering different risk attitudes.

articleTitle: Enhancing the resilience of inverter-dominated power networks via novel distributed secondary integral control
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a novel distributed integral control algorithm is proposed that enhances the resilience of power systems consisting of inverter-interfaced Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). Utilising the structure of the bounded integral controller, the proposed solution achieves frequency restoration, voltage regulation and accurate active and reactive power sharing among the inverters, while inherently satisfying a given apparent power constraint for each inverter via its unique dynamic structure. The boundedness property of the controller is analytically proven using invariance set theory. Furthermore, in the case where one or more inverters reach their apparent power limit as a result of a disturbance (e.g. change in load demand, cyber-attack etc.), the non-compromised inverters restore the grid frequency to its nominal value and continue to share the active and reactive power among them, while the compromised units are automatically excluded from the power sharing procedure, hence enhancing the system resilience. The effectiveness of the proposed controller in achieving the desired control tasks, even in presence of cyber attacks, is validated using a 4-node microgrid with 4 inverter-interfaced DERs created in the Typhoon HIL real time digital simulator.

articleTitle: Analysis of off-grid fast charging stations with photovoltaics, wind turbines, and battery energy storage systems along highways for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Fast-charging stations play a crucial role in the transition to electric vehicles, particularly those located along highways that are expected to replace conventional gas stations. However, these charging stations require significant amounts of electricity due to the high-power demand of the chargers. In some cases, grid availability may be limited or non-existent. This study examines the impact of various capacities of renewable energy sources (RES) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) on charging time and environmental footprint. The simulations indicate that there must be a trade-off between charging time, environmental footprint, and energy rejection, depending on the priorities set by the investor.

articleTitle: A framework for the robotic automation of ultra-high voltage center inspection tasks
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this paper, we present the development of a framework for the task scheduling system to enable the robotic automation of UHVC (ultra-high voltage center) inspection. Equipment failures at UHVC could be significantly reduced if the inspection methodology allowed for condition-based maintenance (CBM) and the equipment status was systematically monitored. To address this, an autonomous mobile robotic vehicle for inspection using an onboard system of optical and thermal cameras has been developed. The framework enables the automatic determination of the inspection schedule based on a combined time-and condition-criterion, the Total Reliability Index (TRI). The TRI represents the probability of equipment failure based on the evaluation of the images obtained through thermal and optical cameras, as well as the component’s age and frequency of inspection, based on its specifications and its importance in the UHVC infrastructure. Depending on the TRI value, a decision is made as to whether a component should be inspected as part of the regular monthly inspection or if it requires more frequent monitoring. The developed framework allows the automated creation of inspection plans on a monthly and weekly basis, based on each component’s TRI and without requiring the user’s input. The framework also enables the user to create inspection plans that can be saved, modified, and scheduled for immediate or future execution. In all cases, the output of the framework is th e list of elements for inspection. The framework enables the execution of systematic, frequent, automated inspections and will lead to financial, administrative and information benefits.

articleTitle: Optimum utilization of renewable energy to generate electricity for chain-markets in Crete
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In large-scale complexes, substantial energy consumption often -results in high operational costs. This issue is especially measurable in commercial and industrial buildings, where HVAC systems and equipment dominate energy usage. Incorporating RES into such complexes aligns with long-term goals of reducing energy expenses and achieving sustainability targets. Supermarkets, in particular, have unique energy profiles due to their operational demands (extended refrigeration requirements and long operating hours). Therefore, careful consideration is required when integrating renewable systems to match their specific energy consumption patterns. Energy storage solutions play a critical role by storing excess energy generated during off-peak periods for use during peak times or when renewable generation is insufficient. This approach not only reduces reliance on expensive grid electricity but also enhances energy resilience. A case study involving a supermarket in Crete demonstrates how optimising photovoltaic (PV) and battery system installation can minimise total energy costs compared to conventional energy setups. The methodology relies on the estimation of hourly electricity consumption, based on recorded monthly values. The building's structural properties were considered alongside a metaheuristic algorithm, the Moth-Flame Optimiser (MFO), which assessed the optimal PV and battery installed capacity.

articleTitle: Positive sequence impedance in three-core armoured cables: measurement and modelling aspects
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Submarine cables are necessary to interconnect offshore renewable projects with the mainland grid. Their geometry typically involves three twisted power cores and an external steel wire armour, which forms a helix and is used for mechanical protection. The positive sequence impedance, namelyZ 1, of such cables is employed in power flow studies and, thus, influences the sizing of the entire project. The Standard-based methods presently used forZ 1calculations, such as that suggested by the CIGRE Technical Brochure 531, rely on semi-empirical formulae which omit the cable helical geometry and ignore the true armour material properties, such as its magnetic permeability. Other methods treating the armour as a pipe, although account for its permeability, fail to capture the so-called “twisting effects” stemming from the helical nature of the cable. State-of-the-art models, capable of incorporating the three-dimensional effects of the induced magnetic field, are used in the present paper and compared against in-house experimental measurements. Various cable samples including all steel grades typically used in practice, i.e., magnetic and non-magnetic alloys, are tested. The proposed models provide results ofZ 1significantly closer to measured data compared to the existing methods, thus facilitating a detailed parametric analysis in a design base.

articleTitle: Dynamic interactions of active distribution network and transmission network at multiple grid supply points
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper is a dynamic study of the interaction between an active distribution network and a transmission network through eight grid supply points at 132 kV. Two different typologies have been adopted for the GSPs connection: radial and mesh. Also, the active distribution network has adopted diverse types of renewable energy resources. In addition, various load models have been adopted to represent several types of low-carbon technologies. Various disturbances have been applied by running electromechanical RMS simulations including three-phase short circuit faults at different locations and at different voltage levels and line outages. The research provides valuable insights into the network's ability to respond to unexpected events when the power network is rich in renewable energy resources and dynamic loads.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis of PV-BESS systems for industrial consumers
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The continuous reduction in renewable energy sources (RES) investment costs creates opportunities for energy consumers to utilize renewable generation and storage to self-generate electricity, thereby lowering their energy costs and limiting their exposure to market price volatility, while at the same time observing strict injection constraints imposed by grid operators. This study investigates the feasibility and optimal sizing of photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to be deployed behind the meter of a Medium Voltage (MV) industrial consumer. A linear programming mathematical optimization algorithm is developed, accounting for the investment cost of the new PV and BESS installations and the cost of energy absorbed from the grid to cover the prosumer’s energy needs. The analysis spans the period from 2025 to 2045, incorporating long term projections of electricity market prices and PV and BESS technology costs. Various energy tariff structures are assessed, including dynamic and static tariffs for grid energy, as well as net-billing (NB) and zero feed-in (ZFI) schemes. To quantify the merit of alternative investment decisions, total prosumer cost over the entire study period are obtained and the levelized energy cost and internal rate of return metrics are computed and compared for all examined cases.

articleTitle: Graph-based impact analysis of cyber-attacks on behind-the-meter infrastructure
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Behind-the-Meter assets are getting more interconnected to realise new applications like flexible tariffs. Cyber-attacks on the resulting control infrastructure may impact a large number of devices, which can result in severe impact on the power system. To analyse the possible impact of such attacks we developed a graph model of the cyber-physical energy system, representing interdependencies between the control infrastructure and the power system. This model is than used for an impact analysis of cyber-attacks with different attack vectors.

articleTitle: Total transfer capacity of the north Greece border: where are we now?
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Nowadays, Regional Coordination Centers (RCCs) promote the coupling of the European electricity markets by performing on a daily basis the Coordinated Capacity Calculation (CCC), that aims to compute the maximum Total Transfer Capacity (TTC) on a secure and reliable way. In this paper, the impact of several factors on the TTC of the North Greece (NGR) border is quantified and presented. More specifically, during 2023 two crucial changes have been applied on the power system of the NGR border. The first change is the energization of the Maritza East - Nea Santa tie-line, which is a second tie-line between Greece and Bulgaria. The second change is the modification of the protection relay settings of the tie-lines between North Macedonia and Greece. These tie-lines are the Bitola - Meliti and Dubrovo - Thessaloniki. The analysis reveals that both changes had a positive impact, increasing considerably the transmission capability of the NGR border.

articleTitle: A two-stage stochastic unit-commitment formulation for evaluating the impact of battery energy storage systems on reserve requirements
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a suitable problem formulation is proposed to evaluate the effect of battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in reducing the reserve requirements of the power system. The problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic unit-commitment problem. In the first stage, the commitment decisions, the energy dispatch and the reserve capacity needs are determined, while the second stage includes decisions that correspond to the real-time operation. The proposed optimization formulation follows a probabilistic approach and estimates the day-ahead reserve requirements that minimize the expected cost based on the uncertainty of renewable energy sources (RESs) generation. Moreover, the upward and downward regulation required to keep balance in the system are integrated for each scenario. To validate the proposed methodology, the updated version of the IEEE RTS 24-bus system for electricity market and power system operation studies is considered. As input data for the simulation, hourly time series provided by the Hellenic Transmission System Operator (TSO) are used to obtain realistic profiles for the RESs generation. An overall reduction in operational cost close to 2% was observed. Moreover, a significant reduction of over 20% was observed in reserve requirements. The results, therefore, indicate that BESSs installation can reduce reserve requirements by mitigating the deviation between forecasted and actual RESs generation.

articleTitle: Biomass top-cycle CHP with high-temperature heat pump coupling: economic insights for industrial decarbonization
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Over half of the final energy consumed by the European industrial sector relied on carbon-emitting fuels in 2022. Biomass-based cogeneration technologies can efficiently adjust to varying industrial electricity and heat demands while contributing to substitute the use of fossil fuels. However, these technologies are best suitable for low-temperature heat applications, such as fuel drying or district heating. This study proposes a biomass cogeneration plant coupled with a high-temperature heat pump as a decarbonization solution for supplying medium-temperature industrial heat. We present an optimization model which combines the operation of cogeneration, heat pump and thermal units. Considering investment and operational costs, results allow us to evaluate the economics of the proposed configuration for a chemical processing industry and contribute to an in-depth understanding of technology options leading to an efficient use of renewable fuels.

articleTitle: Assessing the impact of voltage control schemes on the penetration level of micro-scale hydroelectric power generation in water distribution systems
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: One of the biggest challenges of integrating Distributed Generation (DG) within Power Distribution Systems (PDSs) is to accomplish a maximum generation capacity level, while ensuring operational reliability and service quality. The Hydro-Turbines (H-Ts) in Water Distribution Systems (WDSs), specifically, are DGs that may regulate water pressure while injecting a substantial amount of renewable energy to the PDS. In terms of modeling, they work as links between the WDS and PDS models. In this paper, the impact of centralized and distributed voltage control on the penetration of pressure regulating H-Ts in a PDS, is studied. The two voltage control approaches are incorporated within a co-optimization model that includes both WDS and PDS. Simulation results demonstrate that local intelligent voltage control mitigates many of the disadvantages of currently used Power Factor Control (PFC), without the technical complexities involved in a central control scheme: renewable H-T generation penetration increases, but water pressure regulation does not deteriorate.

articleTitle: Efficient real-time optimal power management of large-scale building prosumers
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: As urbanization accelerates and energy demand increases, buildings continue to be a key contributor to overall energy consumption. Heating and cooling loads, along with the energy needed to produce hot water, contribute almost 60% of the total energy consumption of buildings. Therefore, the need for innovative technologies for smart building energy management systems is more urgent than ever. A method for real-time optimal power management of large-scale building prosumers comprising thermal-electrical loads, electrical loads and plug-in electric vehicles with low computation requirements is proposed in this paper. Thermal and electrical loads are considered flexible, and they are regulated in real time to ensure an economically optimal operation of the building prosumer. The primary goal of the suggested algorithm is to significantly reduce the daily operation cost of the building prosumer while satisfying a wide range of constraints. At the same time effort is paid on achieving power dispatch of the optimal power setpoint in real-time that ensures the highest possible flexibility of building thermal zones and determining the power set-point of the building prosumer and the hosted electric vehicles also in real-time using efficient artificial neural networks.

articleTitle: Data-driven power demand disaggregation to the substation level
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Detailed representations of power systems are critical for understanding the operational characteristics and flexibility offered by smart grid technologies. Many details of power grids, however, remain proprietary assets, limiting the transferability of research results based on reference test networks to the real world. This work develops and validates a new methodology to create representative demand profiles at the transmission substation level. The proposed methodology integrates system demand, power grid, and context layers—each utilizing publicly available data. In the demand layer, K-means clustering captures the core statistical time series characteristics of demand data, increasing computational tractability of the problem. The power grid layer establishes a substation contribution index to system level demand, considering the grid’s network structure. In the context layer, demographic data serve as a proxy of demand. Taken together, the layer information creates a substation demand index, which disaggregates the system level demand profile to each transmission level substation. The method is validated on data from the Alberta transmission system operator (AESO), with results showing a mean percent error around zero, and a maximum percent error at 10%. The hourly, disaggregated substation demand profiles are useful within larger modeling efforts, such as transmission expansion planning and hosting studies.

articleTitle: Energy and cost benefits of advanced lighting technology applications in traffic light systems
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Following a pilot project, which concluded in 2016, the replacement of old energy consuming Traffic Light Systems (TLS) of Nicosia Municipality were the subject of an investigation with regards to the energy saving potential and most importantly the payback period of the investment, through presumptions. This paper presents the results obtained of the new efficient technology implementation, with regards to the energy saving that materialised in the Nicosia Municipality. Investigation is presented in an attempt to determine whether the proposed solution and calculated capital employed had the expected energy usage reduction, return on investment, and payback period. The estimated cost benefit of the installed systems compared to the actual benefits varies significantly, after factors such as maintenance and electricity costs are considered.

articleTitle: A fully co-optimized hybrid approach for short-term PV power forecasting that addresses the challenges of diurnal trends and residuals
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In recent years, intra-day forecasts of PV power generation are becoming increasingly crucial for the optimal operation of modern power systems. In the absence of satellite images and Numerical Weather Predictions, data-driven PV power forecasting models solely rely on on-site numerical measurements, which have been proven sufficient for forecasting horizons up to two hours. This paper introduces a novel, data-driven, hybrid PV power forecasting model for the generation of one- hour ahead forecasts at a minute-scale resolution. The original PV power time-series is decomposed into a diurnal trend and residual components, which are separately handled by Long Short-Term Memory networks and Random Forests, respectively. The proposed model is fully co-optimized using Ant-Lion Optimization, to improve the forecasting accuracy while maintaining the scalability of the overall approach. An ablation study is conducted to assess the performance of the proposed model on real historical data under different weather conditions. The proposed model outperforms all benchmark models under more challenging cloudy conditions, reducing the forecasting error by up to 5.71% and 7.94% regarding the RMSE and the absolute percentage error, respectively, while maintaining the computational efficiency at low levels.

articleTitle: Understanding the impact of weather conditions on the future electrified transportation and distribution grids: a case study of northeast UK under heatwave scenarios
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: To advance towards achieving net-zero emissions targets, governments around the world have established ambitious objectives to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). However, this shift presents significant challenges for the energy sector, particularly the electricity grid. Climate change and extreme weather conditions can exacerbate these challenges. Understanding the impacts of extreme weather is essential for implementing appropriate mitigation strategies, ensuring the adoption of new technologies, such as EVs, can be as effective as possible. This paper examines the impact of EV charging on the electricity grid, focusing on how extreme weather conditions, such as heatwaves, can alter this impact. A model combining lattice Monte Carlo simulations with a roulette wheel mechanism was used to generate diverse EV charging profiles for a high-voltage distribution grid in the North-East UK, projected for 2040. Using the most recent heatwave data, the potential impact of heatwaves was modeled through averaging several scenarios with different severities that impacted the inputs distributions of the proposed algorithms. Case studies revealed that heatwaves have the potential to increase peak demand at specific grid locations, necessitating new strategies for grid management.

articleTitle: Optimal MBU positioning under fault scenario for distribution networks with high PV Penetration
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Faults on distribution networks due to abnormal weather events can lead to disruption and can cause high socio-economic losses. In line with the rising frequency of such events, the paper proposes an algorithm for the optimal deployment of mobile battery units to restore sections of the network. The considered battery units are rated at 1MVA to keep them realistic for the mobi le application. The placement algorithm is formulated as a mixed integer mathematical optimisation problem. Sectionalising / tie switches are assumed on each branch of the network in order to increase the restoration configuration flexibility. Photovoltaic systems, distributed along the network, are allowed to contribute to the restored network sections. A number of critical loads are defined and these are prioritised in the restoration process. The objective function also considers the reduction of the overall renewable energy curtailment. The performance of the algorithm is tested on the IEEE 33 bus network with four tie lines. Scenarios with increasing levels of PV power are considered and the effect of incorporating the PV power is studied.

articleTitle: Data-driven photovoltaic installed capacity detection at low voltage substation level
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems in distribution networks, accurate estimation of PV installed capacity becomes crucial for grid management and planning. This paper proposes a data-driven approach, based on super- vised Machine Learning for estimating total PV installed capacity connected to a Low Voltage (LV) distribution network, using substation level net load measurement data. An XGBoost model is trained to estimate installed PV capacity at the LV side using statistical features from substation net load profiles. Leveraging the availability of residential smart meters, synthetic Medium to Low Voltage substation load profiles are created by sampling and aggregating real consumers’ load profiles, creating a diverse database of synthetic substation load profiles, which is then used to train the model. The proposed methodology is then validated on a synthetic substation dataset generated in a similar manner, demonstrating its effective- ness in accurately estimating PV capacity without the need for expensive and intrusive monitoring equipment. The model performance is assessed in varying degrees of PV penetration and network size, providing a more nuanced evaluation of the proposed model. This data-driven approach provides estimations on unseen synthetic substations with errors of 2.93% and 6.33% for substations with 30 and 150 consumers, respectively, for an actual installed capacity of 150 kWp, which are realistic conditions for European LV networks.

Index Terms: Difference In The Number Of Days

articleTitle: Understanding generator droop voltage control
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Power park modules are required by network codes to provide droop voltage power control at the point of connection (POC) to the grid. This paper contains a thorough analysis of the droop voltage control scheme of power park modules by comparing it with the usual terminal voltage control scheme of synchronous generators in small-test cases. Moreover, it explains the impact of generators under droop voltage control on the power flow solution.

articleTitle: 3-Level Strategy of insulation status monitoring for critical HV motors and generators
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This article summarizes why electrical diagnosis of the stator winding insulation status is a crucial part of the predictive maintenance program for critical HV motors and generators. Furthermore, it elaborates, why a combination of periodic offline testing and online partial discharge monitoring is the most efficient strategy for condition based maintenance of the machine insulation status throughout it´s lifecycle.

articleTitle: Power control strategy of an off-grid PV/battery hybrid system implemented through the V2H concept for improving autonomy and lifespan
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Solar PV/battery systems are one of the well-known and widely used renewable energy systems for the electrification of isolated areas worldwide. Since Photovoltaics output is not stable and varies throughout the day, a battery system is required to store the energy and provide it when needed, at high loads or limited sun. Given the challenges of autonomous operation, battery storage systems are exploited to smooth the supply from PV systems while presenting an operational strategy based on forecasting of power required. In addition, the V2H (Vehicle to Home) technology can be applied, so that an electric vehicle can utilize the excess electricity from the PV for charging, or to provide the necessary power, in order to satisfy the house needs when production is low or the utility electricity price is high. Hence battery depletion or operation at high voltage is avoided so lifespan to be increased. The aim of this study, is the design, control and monitoring of an autonomous solar energy system of 520W of power, operating at 24V through a DC Bus. The supplied power is autonomously determined according the available power from the panels, the total load demand and the batteries’ state of charge (SOC). A rule-based strategy is tested as the hybrid system will be monitored by the Multi Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in order to ensure voltage and frequency regulation. In the results it can be seen, that the battery acts as an auxiliary source for the PV, in order to avoid increased stress caused by high temperatures and constant 100% SoC operation. The MPPT was not active most of the time of the test, as the total 1.2kWh were generated, could easily handle the output required by the AC Bus. In total, battery SoH dropped only 0.3%, which is too low for AGM battery technology. Lastly utilization through the Vehicle to Home (V2H) system where the collaboration of an electric vehicle and this unit ensures maximum energy autonomy for the smart home, EV and PV factors leading to a sustainable off - grid system.

articleTitle: The impact of data time resolution on long-term voltage stability assessment: a case study with offshore wind-solar hybrid power plants
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this study, the impact of data time resolution on long-term voltage stability assessment of a power grid with high penetration of wind-solar hybrid power plants is investigated. Historical and synthetic wind data as well as solar irradiance are used to calculate power output from hypothetical offshore wind-solar hybrid power plants, geographically located off the coast of Massachusetts, USA. The results show that using hourly input data can overestimate the long-term voltage stability, compared with using minute data. However, the relative difference in terms of voltage mean value and standard deviation is marginal whilst the most significant difference is the intensity of the voltage fluctuations. The main drawback of using high-resolution data is the execution time, increasing proportionally with the number of time steps. Thus, it is argued that the choice of da ta time resolution should be based on the aspects of long-term voltage stability and the size of the power grid to be studied.

articleTitle: Hosting capacity within DERMS: seamless integration of distributed energy resources and electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The burgeoning integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), especially electric vehicles (EVs) and intermittent sources like solar and wind, poses significant challenges to distribution grid planning and operations. These challenges are primarily driven by increased demands from EV charging infrastructures and the variability of DER outputs, which can lead to line and cable overloading, voltage fluctuations, and peak load increases. Without strategic planning and integration, these factors may jeopardize grid stability and deter further adoption of EVs and DERs in general. This study introduces an application of Hosting Capacity within Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), designed to assist Distribution System Operators and engineers in effectively accommodating significant integrations of DERs. Through the strategic deployment of the Hosting Capacity application, as part of a broader DERMS planning process, we enable a thorough analysis of the distribution grid's capacity to integrate new charging infrastructures and DER outputs. The efficacy of this integrated approach is demonstrated through a real-world case study, examining the seamless integration of a new 3MW EV charging station and a solar farm of the same size into an existing feeder. This underscores the application's potential to support efficient and resilient grid integration of DERs.

articleTitle: Navigating the impact of huge electrical demand on grid through intelligently controlled renewables and emerging V2G technology
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Among the biggest initiatives to help the UK reach its Net Zero goal are the conversion of the power grid to renewable energy sources (RESs) and the switch to all-electric vehicles (EVs) by 2050. However, because of the advent of dispersed unconventional energy sources and electric vehicles (EVs), the full switch to renewable energy sources and EVs poses a possible risk to power system stability, power quality, and energy management. To intelligently regulate the flow of energy and enhance the current power system, it is crucial to employ appropriate energy management strategies. This paper aims to establish a microgrid that is grid-connected and utilises multiple energy sources, including solar, battery energy storage, and electric vehicles. The goal is to create an intelligent algorithm that efficiently controls these resources and mainly enable bi-directional EV operation for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) application, resulting in both financial and environmental advantages. The main objective is to maximise the microgrid's overall profitability while minimising carbon emissions and effectively managing energy demand and network stability. It has been shown that utilising EVs as storage units via beneficial V2G technology not only stabilises renewable energy generation but also provides economic advantages.

articleTitle: Fault tolerant real time monitored elevator system development
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The paper presents the development of a fault tolerant electromechanical elevator monitoring system aiming to achieve high safety during operation. The proposed methodology is based on a particular permanent magnet synchonous motor (PMSM) in conjunction with suitable driver system characteristics enabling improvements in overall system reliability. The motor design has been performed by using finite elements analysis (FEA) techniques providing detailed operating characteristics of the target motor. Then the motor has been manufactured and appropriately integrated into an existing elevator system in order to validate its operating performance through measurements. The main objective of the drive tuning is to achieve the best possible preventive maintenance of both the motor and the elevator, respectively. For this purpose, real time monitoring and data collection play a key role enabling fault prediction with appropriate techniques and timely information of the maintenance engineer. In this way, the problem can be repaired rapidly, reducing costs and increasing reliability.

articleTitle: Design and tuning aspects of a PSS based on the complete nonlinear synchronous generator model
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: A new insight is given in the analysis of the standard power system stabilizer (PSS) design problem that results in some important methodology novelties. The problem is investigating in a new manner based on the complete nonlinear model of the synchronous generator (SG), in combination with the well-known lead-lag compensator characteristics. According to the deployed theoretical analysis, a novel, simple and reliable PSS design procedure is established that is expected to contribute to the system stability and good response with clearly smooth and fast damping on the local frequency oscillatory behaviour of the SG. Following the proposed methodology, different design and gain tuning cases are examined by conducting extended simulations. All the comparisons between the results, fully confirm the theoretical analysis and indicate the superiority of the proposed design procedure.

articleTitle: Energy usage prediction with ensemble graph convolutional recurrent neural networks: case study of Greek islands
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This study investigates the use of graph convolutional and recurrent neural networks to forecast energy consumption on five Greek islands. The model is trained on historical energy usage data, using graph convolutional networks (GCNs) with graphs constructed from power production and their geographical location which their results are averaged. The evaluation metrics mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) were utilised to measure the accuracy of the proposed prediction algorithms. The results show that all the suggested EGCRNN models with LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and GRU demonstrated excellent performance, strong model fit, and enhanced predictions of energy consumption. In particular, models which utilise long-short term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrence units (GRU) followed with better prediction in one model each, Thira and Rhodes, respectively.

articleTitle: Improvement of reliability performance in distribution network by optimal investment selection
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Distribution system operators often face financial challenges when planning development strategies for distribution networks. These constraints affect decisions about the order and priority of maintenance tasks and the modernization of systems using equipment that incorporates new functionalities. Therefore, it is crucial to systematically and thoroughly analyze the issue and prioritize investment decisions to maximize benefits. This paper analyses the optimal distribution of limited investment funds in order to minimize the Energy not Supplied (ENS) indicator. The choice of investment options is made from predefined actions that include the construction of new power lines to form semi-rings, the replacement of old components with new ones, the replacement of overhead lines with underground cables, as well as installation of remotely operated disconnectors with fault indicators and installation of reclosers. Minimization ofENSis performed for different values of available investment funds. The optimization algorithm was developed and verified on a test system representative of a typical medium-voltage distribution network topology.

articleTitle: Stability boundary analysis of grid-forming and grid-following inverters
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Stability issues and oscillations associated with inverter-based resources (IBRs) are of increasing concern in inverter-dominated power systems. This study explores the stability boundary of grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) inverters and performs a sensitivity analysis for the most relevant control and grid parameters. A stability boundary tracking (SBT) algorithm is proposed, which can identify the stability boundary relating up to three parameters of interest for both GFL and GFM inverters. This boundary is then illustrated as two-dimensional stability curve or three-dimensional stability surface to facilitate understanding the impact of certain parameters on the stability margin. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis of different controller parameters as well as power factor and line R/X ratio draws parallels on their impact to GFL and GFM stability.

articleTitle: Investigation of LSTM-based hybrid approaches for short-term PV power forecasting
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Over the recent years, short-term forecasting models have been proposed and developed in order to deal with continuous penetration of PV power into power systems and maintain their optimal control and operation. Due to the development in technology and the advance of machine learning, hybrid approaches have been considered more and more for the development of power forecasting methodologies, since they are able to optimally utilize the advantages of different methods and thus solve different problems in the forecasting process and improve the total accuracy. This paper introduces and investigates two different hybrid approaches based on the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network and the Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) method. The evaluation of the proposed hybrid approaches considers a seasonal framework and aims to analyse their behavior under the daily weather fluctuations. The proposed Hybrid model 2 is able to outperform all benchmark models considered, improving the forecasting error by 5.79% and 23.79% compared to the LSTM and ARIMA models, respectively, while the proposed Hybrid model 1, manages to surpass the ARIMA model by 18.46%. Both hybrid approaches are able to maintain a low computational burden despite the increase in the complexity of their architecture.

articleTitle: Impact of current phasor measurement configuration on power system state estimation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Current phasor measurements have become increasingly available in modern power systems due to the development of advanced metering systems, including synchrophasor technology. The configuration of these measurements, particularly the installation point of the metering device (whether on a bus or a branch), which determines the measurand (injection or flow), significantly influences the operation of power system state estimators (PSSE). This paper aims to assess the impact of different current measurement schemes on the well-established weighted least squares (WLS) PSSE method, by investigating its performance in terms of convergence and accuracy when using current flow or injection data, as well as a mix of both. Additionally, practical considerations related to technical installation issues, such as the circuit-level measurement point and the utilization of instrument transformers, are discussed. The findings from this analysis demonstrate that the configuration of available current measurements strongly affects the quality of PSSE. Therefore, explicit planning of relevant metering schemes is required to ensure optimal performance.

articleTitle: Maximisation of self-consumption in energy communities
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This research assesses the behaviour of alternative objectives related to maximising the energy self-consumed in renewable energy communities. Three different objective functions are proposed: minimising the grid-supplied energy to the community members, reducing the energy surplus of the community injected into the grid, and maximising the self-consumed energy according to its definition in the Portuguese regulation. Two additional objectives were also considered for comparison purposes, the maximisation of the equivalent CO2 emissions saved and the minimisation of the total community energy cost. The methodology involves formulating and implementing the optimisation problems and discussing the results with a case example, including decreased grid dependency, utilisation of battery storage, and differences in energy trading strategies within the REC. Overall, this research contributes to understanding some alternative objectives that could be considered for the management of the flexible resources of a REC.

articleTitle: Critical comparison of SF6alternative insulating gases and their potential for replacing
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The consolidation of SF<sub>6</sub>, as an insulating gas over the years in electrical distribution and transmission systems, has aided in safety and space occupation, while providing great arc quenching and reliability in medium and high voltage equipment. Aside from its exceptional dielectric properties, SF<sub>6</sub>is extremely harmful environmentally. Using the Global Warming Potential index, which shows the quantity of infrared thermal radiation a gas absorbs after being released into the atmosphere over a certain period of time, SF<sub>6</sub>amounts to 23.500 units. Inevitably so, alternative gases need to be proposed. Therefore, this research article presents and compares suitable, more environmentally friendly, alternative gases to SF<sub>6</sub>. Among the criteria for the comparison, low GWP, high dielectric strength and high electronegativity are of significant importance. Data was carefully selected and verified. Throughout the research, two main categories of possible alternatives were commonly proposed; Perfluorocarbons and refrigerants. Both categories present low GWPs, are highly electronegative and strong dielectrically. Furthermore, they are usually mixed with CO<sub>2</sub>and N<sub>2</sub>. Such perfluorocarbons are C<sub>3</sub>F<sub>8</sub>, CF<sub>3</sub>I and c-C<sub>4</sub>F<sub>7</sub>N and usually perform well when mixed with CO<sub>2</sub>and N<sub>2</sub>. On the contrary, refrigerant gases such as R-134a perform better with a little amount of CO<sub>2</sub>added and are less carcinogenic. However, key – information is still missing for a variety of alternative gases, since some have not been thoroughly researched yet. Generally, most alternatives are less harmful to the ozone layer and perform sufficiently. Further research is needed, however, for their implementation in existing or new equipment.

articleTitle: MIMO impedance modelling of grid following inverter with local voltage control
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In recent years, in response to the global climate crisis, inverter-based energy resources (IBRs) have been massively integrated into power systems. Their effective operation and control lie on a wide variety of inner, outer, and synchronization control loops which have been reported to interact and compromise power system’s stability. In this study, a Multi-Input-Multi-Output (MIMO) impedance model for a three-phase grid following inverter with local voltage control has been proposed. This linear time invariant model takes into consideration the delay and the coupling between the control blocks and serves as a simpler and more computationally efficient method to capture oscillations and interactions in time and frequency domain. It can predict instabilities caused by the different control layers along with the frequencies of the oscillations. The effect of the delay, the current control tuning parameters and the interactions between the current controller and the local voltage controller have been highlighted. The results have been validated in time and frequency domain simulations in SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Inertia of the electric power system with micro grids and renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The paper defines the Coefficient of Accumulated Kinetic Energy (CAKE) as an indicator of the sufficiency of kinetic energy in the rotating masses of thermal and hydro generators that are engaged to cover the power system load diagram. Knowledge of this indicator is of great importance in a situation of increasing engagement of renewable energy sources (RES). The variability of the available RES continuously alters the available inertia of the electricity system, i.e. its available kinetic energy needed to prevent an unwanted drop in the system frequency that occurs immediately after a system power shortage occurs due to generator failure or weather conditions that determine the power output from renewable sources. The calculation of coefficient CAKE was made for the entire power system and for the generators individually. Knowledge of this indicator gives a complete overview of the system's ability to prevent a frequency drop below a certain value (in a concrete analysis, the limit value for the frequency drop is 49.5 Hz). The inadequate value of the CAKE coefficient can be an additional para meter in the short- and long-term generator engagement plan and the quality assessment of theP-fregulation.

articleTitle: Non-linear control with inherent over-current protection for EV charging unit consisting of single active bridge converter
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Active bridge-based chargers for Electric Vehicles (EV) are typically employed in modern power grids in cases where fast, efficient and safe charging conditions are prioritized. Standard control designs for this type of devices usually feature simplistic over-current protection schemes, such as the use of saturation units at the reference current, which are associated with integrator windup and instability phenomena. Contrary to the conventional designs, a novel and model-based Non-Linear Controller (NLC) is proposed for the case of a Single Active Bridge (SAB) fast charger, with a twofold aim: i) to efficiently deliver the desired power to the EV battery through accurate current regulation and ii) to achieve protection of the charging equipment, by inherently limiting the instantaneous converter current below a maximum allowed value without any of the typical drawbacks. This over-current protection property is analytically proved by employing advanced non-linear analysis tools, whereas the stability of the closed-loop system is also guaranteed. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is thoroughly validated on a Typhoon HIL real-time digital simulator by considering different operation cases, including a realistic EV charging scenario (EV charging curve).

articleTitle: Probabilistic small-signal analysis case studies in detailed power system models with converter-interfaced generation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates probabilistic small-signal analysis (PSSA) case studies in a power system permeated with converter-interfaced generation, represented with detailed modelling. The uncertainty introduced by the uptake of renewable energy sources necessitates the use of probabilistic methods in dynamic analysis. PSSA using the Monte Carlo approach can reveal the probability of small-signal instability or ensure small-signal robustness across the operating range, while offering insights into the potential multi-machine interactions that can occur in the system being studied.
