Therefore, case studies are performed in this paper which detail the impact of different heterogeneous generation mixtures (i.e., synchronous generators, and grid-following and grid-forming converters), and the operational timescales of the grid-forming converter controllers, on probabilistic small-signal dynamics and stability of the commonly utilised IEEE 9-bus system.

articleTitle: Zero-voltage-switching conditions for half-controlled secondary-side LLC converter using phase-shift modulation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this article, the half-controlled secondary-side (SS) LLC converter is presented and analysed, along with the boundary conditions for achieving zero-voltage-switching (ZVS). Resonant converters present high-efficiency and power density, minimizing the losses and increasing the overall system efficiency, as well as reducing the electromagnetic interference. LLCs are the most widely used converters of this family and many variations have been proposed in literature for optimizing the operation of specific applications, where usually the switching frequency regulates the output voltage. One of the proposed variations, the SS-LLC, presents a unique topology where the secondary-side bridge is half-controlled, consisting of two diodes and two transistors. While operating at a constant frequency, equal to the resonant, the secondary-side voltage is regulated by the phase difference of the pulses between the two bridges. The proposed topology acts as a boost converter, capable of increasing the output voltage, when necessary, while maintaining commutation under zero-voltage for a wide range of power and voltage output. From the time-domain analysis that is conducted, the boundary conditions for achieving ZVS are derived, based only on the passive components of the converter. The accuracy of the analysis is compared to numerous simulation scenarios.

articleTitle: Unveiling patterns: time series clustering of energy consumption in the Greek energy sector
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In recent years, the energy sector has gathered a lot of attention from researchers to policymakers and industry stakeholders, driven by the goal to improve the sustainability and robustness of energy systems. Central to this discourse is the analysis of energy consumption patterns, as a means to gain a deeper understanding and further improve the load forecasting attempts. Through traditional approaches to energy consumption analysis several limitations emerge, by recognizing them the efforts have shifted to different techniques to unlock the full potential of energy consumption data. Among these techniques, time series clustering emerges as a powerful tool for uncovering hidden patterns, identifying distinct consumption profiles, and informing targeted interventions. By treating energy consumption data as time series sequences, clustering methodologies enable the grouping of similar consumption patterns based on their temporal dynamics, shape, and magnitude. This paper focuses on the methodology, empirical findings, and practical implications of our time series clustering approach for energy consumption analysis. The case study focuses on the Greek energy sector and the clustering of its energy consumption.

articleTitle: Impact of distributed energy resources investment capacities on the carbon footprint of renewable energy communities
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates how distributed energy resources investment capacities impact the carbon footprint of a renewable energy community. The investigation is conducted through the formulation of an optimisation problem minimising an economic (cost) and an environmental (carbon footprint) objectives. It considers new investments and the carbon intensity of energy from the grid. It provides results for grid users acting alone, forming a renewable energy community but investing alone, or allowing co-investment in the community. Multiple case studies are tested to compare the effects of different tariffs and investment budgets. Various locations for renewable energy communities are also tested to see the limitations for profitability depending on the local solar intensity and carbon emission of the external electricity mix. The principal ideas are to demonstrate: that the community framework can reduce the carbon footprint of the system, that a community framework increases the benefits and that an energy bill minimization for all members (maximizing self-consumption) provides an efficient proxy for minimizing carbon footprint.

articleTitle: Forecasting electricity prices for intraday markets using machine learning
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper studies the problem of forecasting electricity prices in continuous short-term electricity markets, specifically focusing on the intraday volume-weighted average price of hourly products in the last three hours of trading. Two state-of-the-art recurrent neural network architectures, namely the Temporal Fusion Transformer and the DeepAR network, are compared against well-established statistical models, such as the Linear Regression – LR, ARX, and SARIMAX models, concerning their forecast accuracy. Historical electricity market and grid data from European Energy Exchanges were used to create a forecasting dataset and train and compare five different model structures stemming from traditional statistical methods or contemporary deep learning-based counterparts.

articleTitle: Impact assessment of the order types mix in the Greek day-ahead electricity market
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The Greek Day-Ahead Electricity Market facilitates a diverse array of order types and offers participants a plethora of choices. While Block Orders are theoretically supported, their accessibility is confined to a subset of market participants so as to ensure the Market Clearing Price formation and the technical feasibility of the resulting Market Schedules. This paper presents a quantitative analysis of the implications of lifting the currently applicable restrictions on the availability of Block Orders in the Greek Day-Ahead Electricity Market, based on past historical data. Clustering techniques are used to convert anonymized past Hourly Hybrid Orders into plausible Block Orders. A market clearing simulator is then used to derive the outcome of the market given the created plausible Block Orders. Simulations are conducted under Coupling and Isolated conditions for three indicative weeks in 2022 and while exploring various scenarios for the specifications of the new Block Orders and the categories of participants who could use them. Assessment metrics encompass Marginal Clearing Price (MCP) statistics, instances of Paradoxically Rejected Block Orders, and Lost Opportunity Cost, shedding light on whether restrictions should be upheld or mitigated.

articleTitle: Cost sharing methodologies for remedial actions in cross-border cooperation between electricity transmission system operators
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The implementation of a methodology for the cost allocation of remedial actions is a necessity for the cooperation of European Transmission System Operators (TSOs). In this study, we adhere to the entirety of the methodology for cross-border congestion management cost sharing developed for the CORE Capacity Calculation Region (CCR) and focus on the variety of power flow decomposition methods that could be used, potentially leading to quantitative differences in the final allocation of congestion management costs. We analyse results from simulating the application of these decomposition methods over a set of test cases based on IEEE benchmarks. Our findings underline the major role of loop flows and reveal that the final cost-sharing outcome is relatively insensitive to the choice of a particular flow decomposition approach. Given that there is no unique answer to the power flow decomposition question, this adds confidence to the cost allocation process envisioned for Europe.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the operational condition of a 150kV power transformer operating in the hellenic electricity distribution system
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Power transformers are vital components of the electricity distribution networks, ensuring the efficient transmission and distribution of electricity across various voltage levels. These transformers, typically operating at high voltages such as 1 50kV, have a crucial function in ensuring the stability and reliability of the power grid. Effective maintenance of them is essential to prevent failures, extend their operational lifespan, and ensure uninterrupted power supply. This paper provides an overview of the critical maintenance practices of power transformers used in the Hellenic Distribution Network for monitoring and enhancing their performance. More specifically, this research has been applied to the 150kV/20kV power transformers installed at the Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network.

articleTitle: Enhanced oscillation damping in power systems by extending the VSI control
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a control scheme is proposed aiming to further support the task of the synchronous generator’s power system stabilizer (PSS) to damp frequency oscillations. The proposed control law is applied as an additional loop to the classical control scheme of the grid-side power converter modelled in thedqsynchronously rotating frame. The main concept is based on suitably varying the dc-link capacitor voltage in order to quickly compensate the oscillating power of the grid. The control method is analysed by deploying a power balance technique which considers both the PSS and the proposed controller main tasks. Inserting the proposed controller into the whole control scheme, the system performance is evaluated through extended simulations on a system consisting of a conventional synchronous generator and a converter powered by a wind turbine, connected to inject power into a local load and the main grid through a transmission line. The examined cases include sudden disturbances occurring in different parts of the system, indicating the enhancement of the oscillations damping and the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Decentralised assessment of future capacities for resource adequacy studies in the European power system
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In addition to weather-dependent renewables, the future power system will also need capacity that can be dispatched at any time to ensure resource adequacy. However, decreasing full load hours and high uncertainties mean that there may not be enough dispatchable capacity available in the future. For this reason, an Economic Viability Assessment is necessary in order to verify whether sufficient dispatchable capacity will be available in the future to ensure resource adequacy. In essence, two distinct approaches can be identified. The first is a centralised approach, which aims to achieve an economic optimum from the perspective of a central planner. The second is a decentralised approach, which determines the economic optimum from the perspective of the numerous individual players within the power system. The present paper employs a decentralised approach to modelling. The model incorporates uncertainties, technological risk and risk aversion. Subsequently, the impact of the resulting increases and decreases in dispatchable capacities on resource adequacy will be analysed. The findings indicate that in the majority of the bidding zones investigated, dispatchable capacities are determined to be uneconomical. Consequently, the resource adequacy parameters also decrease.

articleTitle: Analysis of the renewable energy sources integration in Serbia’s power energy system
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The integration of the renewable energy sources into the power system is a major task for transmission system operators in every country. Big problems can be caused if the analysis of the integration of renewable sources is not done in an adequate way. Great focus must be done towards to this aim. All possible studies must be done in detail. This paper presents exactly one such analysis. It concerns the electric power system of the Republic of Serbia. A realistic problem that can arise in practice is presented and it is taken a step further. There was also a discussion about what would happen if there was a large installation of renewable energy sources. In such cases, big problems can occur with too much energy that has to be exported. The paper analyses two cases: one realistic for the prospective state of 2030 and the other when the installed capacity of renewable sources exceeds consumption. Two software were used for calculations. One is used for calculations at the all country level as one area, and the other calculations that obtain the currents of electricity on each branch and the voltages in each node.

articleTitle: An adaptive phase shedding and interleaving technique for modular dual active bridge converter applied to fast battery charging
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Designing an off-board fast battery charging station is challenging as it must support multiple battery profiles with varying power needs while maintaining high efficiency and compact size. Commonly used modular topologies meet battery power requirements and reduce stress on power switches but suffer from low light-load efficiency. So, this paper proposes an adaptive module-shedding technique that dynamically adds and removes converter modules based on charger power needs, enhancing system efficiency across a wide load range, especially at light load. Additionally, the algorithm includes a PWM phase angle adjustment mechanism to increase input/output ripple frequency, reducing current and voltage ripples. A control technique prevents power imbalance among modules due to parameter mismatches. Numerical simulations in MATLAB/Simulink for an input-parallel output-parallel (IPOP) dual active bridge (DAB) converter confirm the algorithm's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Energy storage capacity credit variation with system adequacy
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates the contribution of energy storage systems to resource adequacy under different power system reliability conditions. To this end, the capacity credit of storage is assessed, assuming different thermal capacity levels integrated in to the system. A reliability-oriented policy for the dispatch of storage is implemented to minimize load curtailments. Storage capacity credit is estimated via the equivalent firm capacity (EFC) metric. The paper demonstrates significant variability in storage capacity credit, contingent upon the level of system adequacy. A consistent trend is observed in the storage EFC as system thermal capacity changes. Specifically, the EFC exhibits low values in two cases: (a) when the system maintains exceedingly high adequacy levels and (b) when it encounters severe inadequacies. Between these extremes, the EFC appears to stabilize around a peak value, thus allowing the identification of the system thermal capacity level at which the storage contribution to adequacy is maximized. Eventually, the analysis suggests that this maximum EFC value can potentially serve as a definitive measure of storage capacity credit.

articleTitle: Optimal PV operation in emergency scenario with virtual inertia provision
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The increased penetration of photovoltaic systems (PVs) into transmission and distribution networks constitutes a step forward in the achievement of sustainable development goals around the world. However, high PV penetration at medium-and low-voltage (LV) distribution networks is associated with voltage violations due to reverse power flows at peak PV generation time and frequency instability caused by the lack of inertia in the system provided by conventional synchronous machines. Solutions to the latter have been explored in literature, mainly on the topic of virtual inertia provision using combined software-hardware solutions. This paper proposes a method to address both voltage violations and frequency instability through a combination of PV active power curtailment and the switching on and off of strategically placed emergency lines tested on the medium-voltage IEEE 22-bus network.

articleTitle: An analysis of social welfare and profitability in VPP bidding strategies on Korean power market
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper focuses on analyzing the market impact of Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) in the Power Market of Korea, with a specific emphasis on social welfare and profitability. Additionally, it evaluates future load trends and assesses business profitability, highlighting the implementation of strategic bidding strategies for VPPs. The case study provides crucial insight for developing policies to mitigate market power and improve social welfare in the participation of VPPs.

articleTitle: Classification method for Li-Ion batteries state of health estimation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In recent years more and more mobile applications are based on electric equipment and on batteries for providing the necessary energy to run them. The most common used battery technology today is the one based on Lithium-Ion. The process of estimating of the state of health for a battery is of high importance for any application based on electrochemical storage. In the last decade, various methods for estimating state of health for batteries have been proposed and studied. In this paper a classification method for estimating the deterioration of a lithium-ion battery is presented and tested on data provided on IEEE DataPort and from measurements carried out for three 18650 lithium-ion batteries. The algorithm applied shows encouraging results, showing a maximal error smaller than 5% for batteries in the interval of state of health between 80 and 100%, an interval where batteries are considered suitable for EVs. Another problem in any application that includes battery management systems, is the lack of documentation regarding the batteries. Besides the state of health estimation, in this paper a method for identifying the documentation of a battery is presented.

articleTitle: Interaction between harmonic current injections from residential loads and electric vehicles in low voltage networks
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The widespread penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) and power electronic-based non-linear residential loads (RLs) in low voltage distribution networks has raised interest in investigating their harmonic interactions and the possibilities for power quality improvement. Harmonic distortion levels in residential feeders are significantly influenced by the phase angle interactions among various harmonic sources, the distribution and locations of harmonic sources, and the intervals of harmonic current aggregation. This paper offers a multi-point analysis of the interactions between harmonic current injections from RLs and EVs, investigating how these interactions can contribute to mitigating harmonic distortion levels in low voltage residential networks. Field measurements, including harmonic current phasors (magnitude and phase) and active and reactive power demands, were conducted for 21 dwellings and 14 different EVs being charged in parking facilities over a one-week period with a temporal resolution of 1 minute in Madrid, Spain. To evaluate the effects of case studies on the harmonic distortion levels and to ensure compliance with power quality benchmarks outlined in the EN50160 standard, these field measurements are injected into the low voltage European test feeder, referred to as LVN#3 - Feeder 5.

articleTitle: Feedback-based safe gradient flow for optimal regulation of virtual power plants
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper considers the problem of controlling distributed energy resources (DERs) in a distribution network (DN); the paper focuses on the voltage regulation task and on the concept ofvirtual power plant(VPP). For the latter, we envision an aggregation of DERs as a VPP that tracks power setpoints at the point of common coupling to provide ancillary services to the bulk power system. We propose a feedback-based controller that pursues solutions to a time-varying AC optimal power flow problem. This controller ensures voltage constraints are met in real time, assuming no voltage measurement errors. The feedback from the system mitigates the controller sensitivity to model uncertainties and eliminates the need for measurements of uncontrollable loads at every node. The feedback-based controller is tested on the IEEE37-node system with delta and wye-connected devices in a strongly unbalanced configuration.

articleTitle: Impact of renewable energy penetration on the Greek distribution network
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper aims to assess the impact of renewable energy penetration on the Greek distribution network. The assessment is performed by using four operation scenarios, characterized by different consumption and generation conditions. To this end, a load flow analysis with typical consumption and generation data is executed and used as a benchmark, whereas the load flow results of the other operation scenarios are compared with the ones of the benchmark case. The comparison is conducted in terms of maximum voltage and possible upper voltage violations, active power losses, active power absorbed, active power generated, and total current in the beginning of the feeder (magnitude and direction, since in some cases there may be inverse power flow from the distribution network to the transmission system). The validation of the results, together with numerical evaluations, are carried out by using a real distribution network feeder of the Greek Distribution System Operator as well as real measurements as input in the load flow analysis. As a further contribution, the paper investigates possible correlations between alarms for instant upper voltage limit violations and the day of the week, the hour of the day, and the typical profile of generation of solar photovoltaic units.

articleTitle: Front-and behind-the-meter storage needs of the Greek power system under high RES penetration levels
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper assesses grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) requirements for the Greek power system, in addition to already scheduled storage projects, aiming to attain upgraded renewable energy penetration targets for 2030. Two alternative BESS integration routes are analyzed, namely front-of-the-meter (FtM) BESSs and behind-the-meter (BtM) BESSs coupled to photovoltaics (PVs) undergoing power output limitations, examining a wide set of storage configurations regarding incurred system benefit. System operation is optimized employing the state-of-the-art unit-commitment and economic dispatch problem, formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming algorithm. The cost-benefit analysis evaluates variable system operating cost reduction due to introduction of storage, as well as the benefit emanating from contribution of additional BESS to system resource adequacy. After deducting annualized cost of additional storage to ensure its economic feasibility, the annual net system benefit is calculated. Energy capacity of introduced BESS configuration is proven determinant of total delivered system benefit. In both storage pathways, similar maximum net benefits can be attained reaching 62-64 million € per annum. Both 1-1.5 GW – 4h of FtM BESSs or BtM BESSs coupled with PVs with 7-10 GWh and 0.5-2 equivalent hours of energy storage capacity deliver similar savings in the vicinity of maximum net benefit.

articleTitle: Residential electrical storage: feasibility study for hybrid residential PV/battery systems in Cyprus
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study on integrating grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems with a potential to implement battery storage in residential settings. It analyses the performance and feasibility of such systems in enhancing self-consumption and energy export. The simulation model considers factors like household energy demand profiles, and PV output profiles. Through this analysis, it is anticipated to offer insights for homeowners, policymakers, and industry stakeholders on achieving greater energy independence and resilience. Finally, findings show that the attempt to effectively utilise battery storage in a residence while aiming for the most economically feasible system heavily depends on the load demand. It was observed that no matter the profile of the building or the energy utilisation, there is no significant change in energy costs. However, the results manifested an upcoming trend for utilising energy that will prove beneficial for costumers.

articleTitle: Coupled electromagnetic-thermal modelling of 3D-printed iron core of high speed PM motor
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (also known as 3D-printing) is opening up new ground for innovations in customizable, scalable and cost-efficient motor design solutions. The continuous effort to improve the efficiency and reduce the production costs of electric motors has led researchers to search for new and innovative manufacturing techniques. Such a new technique enabling construction of electric motor parts is 3D printing. The production of mechanical components by means of 3D printing, although is actually at an early stage of adoption, seems to offer important advantages. Thus, the interest of the research community in determining the quality, reliability and performance of 3D printed motor parts grows rapidly, focusing o n challenges that are related to the design and construction of high-speed motors with high efficiency and power density. This paper presents the thermal analysis of a particular 3D-printed magnetic iron material (which is commercially available) used for the design and manufacturing of the stator core of a low-power and high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor. The findings of the simulations were confirmed experimentally.

articleTitle: Estimating the real contribution of wind parks on covering the Greek mainland load demand
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: During the last ten years, there is a significant wind power increase in the national electricity generation fuel mix, since the current (end of 2023) national installed wind power capacity exceeds 5.2 GWe in comparison with the 1.9 GWe of 2013. Moreover, according to the revised NPEC (October 2023) the expected wind power by 2030 may exceed 9.5 GWe. Although this continuous wind power time evolution seems to favour the clean-green electricity production, significant wind power absorption problems have been appeared during the last two years. Keep also in mind that the average annual load demand of the mainland electrical system (2023) is approximately 5700 GWe, a value that is comparable with the already installed wind power capacity. In this context, the proposed work presents a detailed hourly statistical analysis of the Greek wind parks participation to cover the mainland load demand for the period 2016-2021. This specific period has been selected since during this period there was not any systematic wind power curtailment, hence it may be used to estimate the real capacity credit of the wind power in the national electricity generation system (EGS). Using the proposed analysis, the hourly contribution of the wind energy in the national EGS has been investigated and the capacity credit of the existing wind parks has been estimated on monthly and annual basis. On monthly basis, the minimum capacity credit values have been encountered from April to July, while the maximum values appear mainly during winter. Consequently, on annual basis, the average capacity credit is slightly higher than 20%, while a deceasing trend has been observed as the installed wind power is increasing.

articleTitle: Analytical design of a DC FCL reactor for pole-to-pole fault current in an MMC-based 2-terminal DC grid
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In the case of DC grids, the fault characteristics differ from those of conventional AC system and vary depending on the converter configuration and type of fault. Additionally, for modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based DC grids, the parameters of the MMC influence the rate of change and maximum values of fault currents. This paper proposes an analytical calculation of pole-to-pole fault currents and the calculation based DC FCL reactor design for MMC-based symmetrical monopole DC grids. The calculation involves solving circuit equations in the time domain to derive mathematical expressions, using MMC fault equivalent model. This calculation enables accurate and fast computation by providing fault current expressions based on circuit parameters. The calculation result is validated through PSCAD/EMTDC simulations.

articleTitle: Advanced grid inspection methodologies for enhancing electrical infrastructure in Greece
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The electrical grid is vital to modern society as it enables the seamless distribution of electricity to power homes, businesses, and industries. However, it is a system that is constantly being modified: the energy demand is increasing due to population g rowth, urbanization and technological developments. Furthermore, there is a constant demand for grid expansion in order to install more RES units to meet the zero emission targets by 2050 and to address congestion issues. Therefore, the assurance of the reliability and resilience of the grid is of paramount importance and ensuring the grid's integrity and efficiency requires the implementation of advanced inspection methods of its components, capable of identifying vulnerabilities, mitigating risks, and optimizing performance. The combination of automated drone inspections, AI algorithms for fault detection and the tools for grid digitization offer a comprehensive solution to the inspections and maintenance problems, and a great opportunity for the Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) to improve upon the current practices.

articleTitle: An investment prioritization model for wildfire risk mitigation through power line undergrounding
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Grid-ignited wildfires are one of the most destructive catastrophic events, profoundly affecting the built and natural environments. Burying power lines is an effective solution for mitigating the risk of wildfire ignition. However, it is a costly capital expenditure (CapEx) requiring meticulous planning and investment prioritization. This paper proposes a systematic approach to estimate the potential wildfire ignition damage associated with each transmission line and accordingly offers a priority list for undergrounding. The proposed approach allows electric utilities to make risk-informed decisions for grid modernization and resiliency improvement against wildfires. As a case study, we examine the likelihood of wildfire ignition for each line segment, i.e., between two high-voltage towers, under diverse weather conditions throughout the year. The studies on the standard IEEE 30-bus test system, simulated on 43,712 scenarios, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Energy saving, enhanced public safety, and improved quality of life with sensor based street lighting systems enabled by IoT technologies
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Street lighting is vital for urban infrastructure, ensuring public safety, security, and aesthetic appeal. Traditional system s often face inefficiencies and limitations, failing to meet the dynamic needs of modern cities. Integrating sensors and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies offer a transformative solution, modernizing and optimizing street lighting. This paper reviews recent advancements in sensor-based street lighting systems enabled by IoT. It explores the role of sensors and IoT platforms in revolutionizing street lighting, leading to smarter, more responsive solutions. The initial section highlights the significance of street lighting in urban environments and the challenges of traditional systems, such as energy inefficiency and inadequate responsiveness. The integration of sensors and IoT technologies is examined, showcasing their potential to optimize energy consumption, reduce operational costs, and enhance user experience. Practical implementations and case studies are analysed, providing insights into successful deployments and operational challenges. The paper concludes by examining the potential impact of sensor-based street lighting systems on urban environments. Benefits include substantial energy savings, reduced carbon emissions, enhanced public safety, and improved quality of life. However, challenges such as scalability, interoperability, data privacy, and security are also acknowledged.

articleTitle: Intelligent management of integrated energy systems in remote maritime environments utilizing fuzzy modes
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper explores isolated maritime environments equipped with an integrated energy system (IET) to fulfil the energy requirements of nearby communities. These environments are presumed to lack grid access but possess a connection point for a floating energy source capable of supplying consistent electricity for a limited duration. The study introduces a novel management system for the efficient operation of IES in such environments, utilizing an innovative multi-mode approach. Specifically, the system includes several management modes, each employing a distinct management strategy for the IET. These modes are implemented using fuzzy logic tools, with a core of IF/THEN control rules that enable flexible and rapid decision-making. The fundamental concept is that the use of modes in decision-making inherently prioritizes specific operational objectives and consumption needs based on current conditions. The proposed system comprises three modes and is tested through a series of simulated scenarios. Results indicate that the IET can provide flexible energy management that adapts to dynamic conditions, outperforming a single-strategy system.

articleTitle: Comparison of black and white box model of VSC by DQ-frame admittance modeling method
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation method of voltage source converter (VSC) admittance modeling in the dq frame, divided into white-box and black-box models, and compares the results of the two models to validate the black-box model. For the VSC admittance modeling of the white-box model, the small-signal modeling technique is applied to reflect the dynamic characteristics of the phase-locked loop. The harmonic injection method and vector fitting method were applied to model the VSC admittance of the black-box model using PSCAD/EMTDC simulation. The results of this study confirm that the black-box model can reproduce the dynamic characteristics of the VSC, with results that are quite similar to those of the white-box model. This study will serve as an important foundation for future VSC modeling research.

articleTitle: Semaptic, a new semantic framework for fast and easy interoperability and its application to energy services
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Ensuring robust semantic interoperability is essential for efficient data exchange in the energy sector. This paper introduces SEMAPTIC, a lightweight framework that simplifies semantic interoperability by providing a standardized approach for attaching metadata to exchanged data. SEMAPTIC utilizes ontologies to define the meaning of data elements and employs a new structured metadata map to guide data interpretation. This approach simplifies data exchange, minimizes maintenance effort, and fosters unambiguous data understanding across heterogeneous systems. Compared to traditional methods that often require complex data transformations, SEMAPTIC offers greater flexibility and reduced overhead. The paper explores the benefits of SEMAPTIC, including simplified integration, minimal maintenance, enhanced interoperability, reduced misinterpretation, facilitated data reuse, and future-proofing. A practical example showcases how SEMAPTIC enriches a JSON data structure with semantic context without the need of modifying the original structure and without inflating data size. Finally, the importance of well-defined ontologies is emphasized, highlighting how SEMAPTIC empowers the energy sector to achieve seamless and reliable data exchange, paving the way for a more efficient and intelligent energy ecosystem.

articleTitle: Optimization and performance of bifacial PV system compared to monofacial
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of a bifacial photovoltaic (BFPV) system with a monofacial (MFPV) one, installed on the rooftop of the Polytechnic University of Tirana, Albania (choosing the same size of 168 kWp). The row spacing is 1.9m, the PV height is 0.3m, and the orientation is to the south (1680). The simulations show that the BFPV system performs better every month, increasing the annual PV Energy by 8.3%. Furthermore, to find the optimal design, the impact of tilt angle, elevation, and albedo on the Specific Annual Yield of the BFPV system is studied. Keeping the orientation and the row spacing unchanged, it turns out that the optimal tilt angle is 250 (against 280 in the MFPV system), the optimal height is 0.3 m, and the optimal albedo value is 0.9 (white surface). Comparing it with the optimized MFPV system, this configuration would give a gain of 15.7%. However, for albedo values up to 0.35, the optimal tilt angle for BFPV is 200. On the other hand, using a regression analysis (considering R2 and P-value) through the obtained results, Specific Annual Yield and Bifacial Gain (BG) are expressed as a third-order polynomial equation depending on the above parameters.

articleTitle: Design and monitoring of a large data center lightning protection system
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The number of built objects of large data centers (DCs) rapidly increasing. High quality protection of equipment and devices and, above all, the services that the DC provides, becomes imperative. The application of DC object protection measures against lightning is becoming more and more effective. In this paper are explained methods for implementation of lightning protection system based on international standards and solution that separate bonding mesh in the form of internal Faraday cage from conductor system and earth termination system realized in the form of external Faraday cage. By continuously measuring values of essential parameters, data processing and information storing, as well as using computer network of the DC itself and existing monitoring and management system, enables real-time lightning protection system condition visibility.

articleTitle: Assessment of the impact of HVDC systems on power system restoration
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This research investigates the role that High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) technology could play in power system restoration. Typically, the need of system restoration occurs following extreme events that lead to a blackout of a power system. In such cases, it is important to restore the system load as fast as possible. System operators mainly procure black-start services from conventional generating units, that progressively energise the transmission network, build a skeleton from their terminals to other generating units and, eventually, the load. This energisation is subject to several network and ramp-up constraints of the generating units. Past studies have formulated the restoration of the system as an optimisation problem that aims to minimise the load supply interruption. This work extends on the existing framework, by integrating HVDC systems into the formulation and applying it to support the restoration, either through transfer of power or by using the converters as black-start units. The proposed formulation accommodates various HVDC configurations that can arise. Simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus system reveal that significant benefits can be obtained by the utilisation of HVDC links during black-start.

articleTitle: Integrating third-party flexibility resources into distribution networks: a quantitative assessment on the interactions of network tariffs and local markets
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper explores innovative approaches to enhance the use of flexibility for electrical distribution networks by integrating time-of-use tariffs and local markets for DSO services. The study presents an analysis through a case study of three distinct scenarios. The first scenario examines the impact of the simultaneous operation of heat pump and electric vehicle loads, leading to significant congestion issues within the network. It highlights the challenges posed by the increasing presence of flexible loads without any pricing signals to guide their operation. In the second scenario, price signals based on time block and contracted capacity charges are introduced, demonstrating how these signals can effectively alleviate network congestion but could shift problems to other hours. The third scenario combines the benefits of tariffs with a local market, resulting in the most significant reduction in grid congestion. Consequently, the outcomes of the current analysis could support regulators and policymakers in designing efficient acquisition mechanisms tailored to the characteristics of the context to which they apply.

articleTitle: Reconnection of MV microgrid with universal grid-forming inverter-based resources
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: One concern of typically proposed grid-forming (GFM) inverter-based resources (IBRs) has been the microgrid reconnection i.e. transition from islanded to grid-connected operation. Therefore, this paper presents a case study about medium-voltage (MV) microgrid reconnection with universal frequency-locked-loop (U-FLL) -based GFM IBRs. The main aim of the PSCAD simulations was to find out that what is the maximum allowed voltage phase angle difference before MV microgrid reconnection to maintain stability of U-FLL-based IBRs after the reconnection and how much it is dependent on the simultaneous frequency and voltage magnitude differences. Based on the simulation results, the U-FLL based IBRs have very good voltage phase angle difference ride through capabilities i.e. ±140-180° depending on the case. Paper also proposes one new scheme in which perfectly synchronized reconnection could be always achieved by having U-FLL input of one MV IBR from a utility grid synchronous generator’s rotating speed. In addition, paper presents further modified and improved U-FLL-based synchronization method which is grid-forming for generating IBRs and grid-supporting for IBR-based loads.

articleTitle: Synthetic minority oversampling technique for synthetic meteorological data generation*
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This study investigates different approaches for synthetic data generation of time series. The main focus of this study is the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) model, which is widely applied in several situations due to its particular ability to deal with unbalanced datasets. In order to assess the effectiveness and accuracy of different models, a comparison between them is performed. In particular, the SMOTE model is applied using two datasets from the Pinhão Region and Quinta de Santa Bárbara, being applied to the analysis and generation of several different variables, namely, Average temperature, Wind direction, Average wind speed, Maximum instantaneous wind speed and Solar radiation. Through the use of SMOTE it was possible to generate missing data in Quinta de Santa Bárbara in the period from September to December 2022, resulting from this process an analysis of the results and a comparison with the results obtained with the Linear Regression Method and the Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) model. Thus, with this study, the SMOTE model demonstrated good results in the synthetic generation of the missing data, making it a viable option for the function.

articleTitle: Wind energy calculations and hydrodynamic analysis of a 20 MW floating wind turbine
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates the behavior of a floating wind turbine, under irregular waves. It provides a thorough description of the geometrical characteristics of the floating body and the results in terms of the incident waves. Details concerning the modeling of the system are discussed, whereas numerical results obtained in the frequency domain are presented. The floating structure, which is exposed to the action of regular and irregular waves in finite-depth waters, encompasses a semi-submersible offshore floating structure, moored with conventional catenary mooring lines, supporting a 20 MW Wind Turbine. The analysis aims to investigate which sea states yield the significant wave loads of the offshore structure, due to operating wave conditions, obtained through wave hind-cast time series in the Mediterranean Sea. Finally, the annual energy output of the 20MW Wind Turbine is presented.

articleTitle: Towards a comprehensive framework for cyber-incident response decision support in smart grids
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The modernization of power grid infrastructures necessitates the incorporation of decision support systems to effectively mitigate cybersecurity threats. This paper presents a comprehensive framework based on integrating Attack-Defense Trees and the Multi-Criteria Decision Making method to enhance smart grid cybersecurity. By analyzing risk attributes and optimizing defense strategies, this framework enables grid operators to prioritize critical security measures. Additionally, this pap er incorporates findings on decision-making processes in intelligent power systems to present a comprehensive approach to grid cybersecurity. The proposed model aims to optimize the effectiveness and efficiency of grid cybersecurity efforts while offering insights into future grid management challenges.

articleTitle: Electric bus as a service: techno economic evaluation of e-Bus procurement models
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The ongoing market revolution in the automotive sector about the development of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is involving not only European car manufacturers, but also European Countries. Despite the technical challenges related with this topic and the different solutions adopted, the greatest difficulty stands with the customer experience, of which procurement is one of the most critical components. The EVs market already offers several solutions represented by different vehicle characteristics and performances. This paper presents an assessment of electric bus procurement approaches by means of a multi-criteria analysis. The analysis is based on techno-economic Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), to lead the decision-making process in implementing the e-Bus-as-a-Service (e-BaaS) model. An extensive review of the main characteristics of the e-BaaS model is conducted and the procurement models presented in five scenarios considered are assessed. A sensitivity analysis is also provided, to validate the multi-criteria tool. Results point out that e-BaaS can be a feasible way in a future perspective for Transport Operators (TOs) that are called to provide mobility services given particular boundary conditions, either financial or environmental.

articleTitle: Investigation on electrical discharge growth over solid insulating surfaces using a 3D fractal-based model
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This study presents a 3D fractal-based model to simulate the growth of surface discharges considering streamer branching. The model integrates stochastic characteristics of discharge growth by using a fractal algorithm, implemented in MATLAB, alongside electrostatic field computations via COMSOL Multiphysics. Literature experimental results on surface discharges in a needle-plane electrode bridged by insulating specimens are used to check the effectiveness of the developed model. Simulation results are in satisfactory agreement with the literature experimental data on the basis of fractal dimension. The model is a promising tool for enhancing the design and safety of insulation systems in electrical applications.

articleTitle: Investigation into the impacts of self-inductance and mutual inductance on saggy winding inductive coupling power transmission
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of self-inductance and mutual inductance on saggy coil magnetic resonant inductive coupling power transmission (IPT). The simulation of the saggy coil is conducted using a specialist tool called IPTVisual to visualise the phenomenon of saggy winding in the system. The results provide important intuitions for optimising saggy coil inductive coupling devices for better performance and reliability in a variety of applications. The setup of simulations and experimental shows a slight difference. The mutual inductance and coupling coefficient of two saggy coils are analysed and discussed. There is a difference of 1.74% in self-inductance in saggy coil with two fixed mounting point of 1 m distance when comparison is made between simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Hosting capacity calculation of photovoltaic penetration in a closed loop distribution network: a case study
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Investment in photovoltaic plants (PV) by consumers in the low voltage (LV) distribution grid requires special attention regarding their impact on the existing network. Depending on their capacity, these microgenerators can produce enough energy to meet their own needs as well as feed energy into the network, generating extra incomes in the process. The current network was not designed with these PV microsources in mind, therefore connecting them indefinitely could lead to operational and technical issues. The calculation of a maximum value known as Hosting Capacity (HC), that will penetrate the system without negatively affecting the network parameters is necessary to ensure safe operation and management in the future. This value is computed in a closed loop distribution (CLD) network type from Durres region of Albania, accounting for losses, voltage level, element loading and harmonic distortion. The PV penetration of these microgenerators value is approximately 60% of the grid's maximum load, with harmonic distortion of the voltage acting as the limiting factor.

articleTitle: Energy production forecast for the purpose of a technical virtual power plant
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper outlines a comprehensive project aimed for energy management within the facilities of the Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje (UKIM) through the design of a Virtual Power Plant (VPP). So far, there has been no unified standard for a VPP operation. The VPP concept involves integrating distributed energy sources, electricity storage systems and VPP management system. An analysis of datasets for: i) electricity consumption at UKIM facilities, ii) online data from „photovoltaic geographical information system“ for solar radiation in Skopje, and iii) electricity production of photovoltaics (PVs) placed on the roof of one faculty, were carried out. Furthermore, a statistical time series forecasting approach using measured histori cal data (ARIMA) was employed to predict energy production from PV systems intended for installation on other university facilities. Additionally, this paper proposes an approach for forecasting energy production from photovoltaic systems within the VPP framework, contributing to the advancement of sustainable energy management practices in academic institutions.

articleTitle: Grid-following and grid-forming technology options for Corinth - Kos HVDC interconnection
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The Corinth-Kos MMC VSC HVDC link will interconnect the Dodecane complex of islands with the mainland Hellenic Electricity Transmission System (HETS) and will need to operate either in parallel to a weak AC interconnection or even as the only grid-forming resource of the Dodecane interconnection. This paper analyses the options of operating the HVDC converters at Kos Island either in grid-following (GFL) or in grid-forming (GFM) mode. While both options are feasible, they necessitate different types of reinforcements. The GFL option necessitates the presence of local resources such as synchronous condensers but it does not require a Dynamic Braking Module (chopper), which is necessary in the GFM case. It is also shown that the GFM option can facilitate the coordination of the HVDC active power recovery after a fault with RES plants that are planned to be installed in the Dodecane area.

articleTitle: A local control of interlinking DC/DC converters in DC microgrid clusters for global power sharing
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: A new local control strategy for global power sharing (GPS) of islanded DC microgrid (DCMG) clusters is proposed to achieve efficiency and reliability. In the proposed method, power reference of interlinking DC/DC converters (IDCs) are determined to equalize DC voltage levels for both sides. Different from the conventional proportional integral (PI) controller-based control scheme, the proposed method can be implemented for multiple IDCs in a stable manner. The stability of the proposed method is assessed by developing a small-signal state-space (SS) model of the test system and conducting an eigenvalue analysis. Further- more, selection philosophy of appropriate parameters for the proposed control scheme is provided. Finally, the proposed method is validated through electro-magnetic transient (EMT) simulation and is compared to that of the conventional method.

articleTitle: Impact of fires and smoke on the development and occurrence of short circuits and secondary fires in electricity transmission and distribution networks. a review
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: In modern times, there is a significant increase in fires caused in an electricity transmission and distribution network worldwide. These fires are mainly due to the existence of short circuits and secondary factors, due to smoke growing above the ground. As a result, the fire continuously heats the air, increasing the possibility of decomposition. Smoke, composed of carbon particl es, creates conductive paths between transmission lines as well as ground lines. The smoke combined with the heat generated, reduces the dielectric strength, which increases the bend line arrow and the air gap breaks down. In this work, the causes, the effects of fires and the means to prevent and face them are first analyzed with the help of scientific research that speciali zes in the aforementioned issues. In addition, the heating mechanism of air by fire is examined, the components of the generated smoke and how it destroys the layers of insulation, and how the fire affects the transmission and distribution pylon of electricity . Finally, additional factors that contribute to the existence of fires and smoke are successively identified and the consequen ces created are mentioned. In parallel to the theoretical analysis of the phenomenon, follows the experimental process - modeling, this leads us to draw very useful conclusions for future processes and research.

articleTitle: A robust optimization formulation for the integration of photovoltaics in a low-voltage distribution network: Malta case study
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The Maltese islands’ high solar irradiance makes them an ideal location for photovoltaic systems (PVs), offering significant potential for sustainable and decentralized power generation. In the context of low-voltage (LV) distribution networks, various studies utilizing stochastic analyses have linked an increase in PV penetration with voltage violations at load buses and line thermal limit violations resulting from reverse power flows through the feeder head. Despite these challenges, real-time active network management (ANM) solutions for addressing such issues have been underexplored. This paper introduces a robust optimization approach coupled with the open-source tool Open-DSOPF to obtain quantitative data on how PV active power generation may be curtailed to ensure a network can stay within the nominal operational limits. Real smart-meter load and PV profile data is used in the simulation, ensuring accurate modelling of a Maltese LV feeder from the island of Gozo. Open-DSOPF is used to perform a three-phase unbalanced optimal power flow seeking to minimize PV active power curtailment. Results show that curtailment is positively correlated with the total feeder path length to load buses at which PVs are present.

articleTitle: Grid-assistive use of private battery energy storage systems based on fuzzy logic
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The energy transition is changing the structures of the electrical grid. The increasing number of decentralised energy generation systems, especially private photovoltaic (PV) systems, as well as high-power electrical loads in the low-voltage (LV) grid are leading to overloads at the local grid transformer in both power flow directions. This can lead to protection, reliability, stability and voltage quality problems. This paper investigates whether these overloads can be reduced by the grid-assistive use of private battery energy storage systems (BESS), which are installed in households in combination with a PV system. For this purpose, a real LV grid with a high density of PV systems is simulated. Fuzzy logic is used to develop a control system for the BESS installed in the grid based on a 24-hour power forecast. The results show that the control can reduce normal power peaks by up to 33.1% respectively reverse peaks by up to 16.1 % and fully utilise the storage capacity. When considering future grids, however, it becomes clear that the presented method does not offer a complete alternative to grid expansion, but rather enables a delay in grid expansion.

articleTitle: Voltage regulation system in LV networks with high level of renewables and electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a single-phase low-voltage regulator (LVR) prototype aimed at addressing voltage variations at the point of common coupling (PCC) in residential dwellings. These variations are increasing due to the rapid integration of private photovoltaic systems (PVs) and electric vehicles (EVs) into LV networks. The device being proposed operates on the series compensation concept, utilizing two different fixed-ratio transformers that are intelligently switched to achieve the necessary voltage correction. The primary design objectives of the regulator are simplicity, reliability and cost-effectiveness. This work discusses the hardware and testing of a developed prototype and presents the preliminary laboratory testing results.

articleTitle: Principles and approaches for successful energy transition
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The countries with electricity generation based on fossil fuels have questionable future energy independence and security of end-users supply. Hence, it is inevitable to find technical and technological solutions that will enable sustainable future development. A holistic approach, proposed in this paper, could enhance the synergy of the solutions and various options for power systems’ long-term decarbonization and operational optimization in real time. That approach comprehends, among others, the application of circular economy principles, improvement of energy efficiency and the system’s flexibility, diversification of primary fuels and types of energy sources, multifunctional utilization of the primary fuels and efficient energy conversion and storage, utilizing the electricity surpluses. It is necessary to establish gradually such a production mix, which would be based and relied on different, environmentally friendly energy sources and on new technologies, which will be not only feasible and sustainable in the long term, but also technically, financially and economically optimal, as well as social ly acceptable. The principles that will lead to an increase in energy efficiency, the establishment of a circular economy in the power sector and the reduction of its negative impacts on the environment, as well as on the social aspect, should be respected and applied.

articleTitle: Optimal combination of stochastic renewables installation
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The optimal installation of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) constitutes one of the main research topics related to the ongoing energy transition and the efficient utilization of resources. This paper presents an adaptable optimization algorithm for the optimal selection of various stochastic RES, such as Photovoltaic (PV) systems and Wind Generators (WGs), knowing the production profile of each type of RES and the limitations related to its size. The purpose is to define the optimal combination that minimizes the mismatch between the total RES production to be installed and the load curve. The main advantages of the algorithm are that it can perform calculations with high resolution for large time intervals, e.g., a representative year, it may take any number of RES types into consideration and is completely open source, meaning that the solver behind the optimization model is developed as well. The algorithm is applied to a power system that considers the installation of three different types of stochastic RES with an hourly resolution for one representative year in order to highlight its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Assessing the impact of RES on the grid of autonomous electrical systems using representative operation scenarios: the case of Chios Island
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The incorporation of renewable energy sources (RES) in the power generation mix can be beneficial for the energy transition towards a cleaner energy mix, however, from a technical perspective, their connection to the grid is not without its drawbacks. Small-scale RES units that are dispersed along the distribution network are likely to provoke voltage and overloading issues, if their connection is not studied properly. To overcome such issues, distribution system operators (DSOs) should carry out detailed grid impact studies, which, in turn, require adequate data that in many cases are not available, and timeseries that are not always given in a granular chronological basis. In that context, DSOs should rely on the available data, even inadequate, to form representative, yet realistic scenarios to capture the coincidence of extreme conditions regarding load and distributed generation. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology that opts for representative scenarios to assess the operation of the medium voltage (MV) distribution network in autonomous electrical systems with increased RES penetration. The proposed methodology is applied to a real-world case, that of the distribution system of Chios Island, to resolve grid issues and to examine the hosting capacity of new hybrid power stations.

articleTitle: Identifying critical components in power networks through machine learning
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: As modern power systems become more complex, identifying critical components for their reliable operation is becoming increasingly important, especially in dealing with widespread cascading outages from large-scale disturbances. In this context, this paper introduces a novel method for identifying critical components in terms of their contribution to cascading-induced demand not served (DNS), utilizing feature selection techniques integrated with a machine learning classifier model. While existing methods predominantly identify critical assets using DNS, they often overlook the effects of cascading failures. Furthermore, those that do consider cascading failures typically focus solely on line overloading. This work, therefore, introduces a machine learning-based methodology coupled with a cascading failure model, considering protection mechanisms like excitation limits, under/over frequency, and line overloading. Tested on the IEEE 24-bus system, the validation method exhibits strong sensitivity (80.35%-90.03%) and specificity (80.35%-94.10%). Additionally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is used for validation by comparing its results with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Privacy-preserving energy theft detection based on federated learning
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes a secure and privacy-preserving framework for detecting unauthorized energy usage by leveraging consumer energy consumption data in smart grids. Addressing the limitations of traditional centralized schemes, a secure privacy-preserving federated learning framework, named Paillier-Encrypted Federated Learning-based Detection (PE-FLD), is adopted. This architecture consists of a global centre and multiple local detection centers, which interact solely with local consumer data and subsequently communicate aggregated parameters to the global center, thereby safeguarding user privacy. Furthermore, a modified Transformer Neural Network is employed for energy theft monitoring in smart meters. Experimental validation is conducted using real energy consumption data from the Irish Electricity Metering Dataset.

articleTitle: Impact of demand uncertainties on the optimal design of the integrated energy system: determining no-regret infrastructure needs
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The climate policy goals require a fundamental transformation of the energy system, including a shift from fossil fuels to re- newable energy sources. At the same time, the energy system must be able to reliably meet the future demand for various energy carriers. This raises the question of which infrastructures are needed to meet the future supply task in the energy system. Due to the required speed of the transformation, decisions regarding necessary infrastructures must be made already today. However, uncertainties concerning future developments make these decisions more difficult. Especially the future demand structure is highly uncertain. In this context, the paper investigates how uncertainties in the future demand structure affect the resulting needs for expanding generation and transport infrastructures in a sector-coupled energy system. To adequately reflect the un- certainties, a wide variety of scenarios for the future demand structure is examined. Furthermore, this paper presents a no-regret approach for incorporating uncertainties in the determination of infrastructure needs. This approach is then applied to an energy system optimization model in order to identify infrastructure technologies and capacities that will be needed regardless of the considered future developments. The investigations indicate that uncertainties in the demand structure have a major impact on the no-regret capacities of sector-coupling technologies, especially on electrolysis capacity. In contrast, uncertainties have less impact on the capacities of renewable energy plants, which results in higher no-regret capacities.

articleTitle: Empowering aggregators with practical data-driven tools: harnessing aggregated and disaggregated flexibility for demand response
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: This study explores the interaction between aggregators and building occupants in activating flexibility through Demand Response (DR) programs, with a focus on reinforcing the resilience of the energy system considering the uncertainties presented by Renewable Energy Sources (RES). Firstly, it introduces a methodology of optimizing aggregated flexibility provision strategies in environments with limited data, utilizing Discrete Fourier Transformation (DFT) and clustering techniques to identify building occupants’ activity patterns. Secondly, the study assesses the disaggregated flexibility provision of Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems during DR events, employing machine learning and optimization techniques for precise, device-level analysis. The first approach offers a non-intrusive pathway for aggregators to provide flexibility services in environments of a single smart meter for the whole building’s consumption, while the second approach maximizes the amount of flexibility in the case of dedicated metering devices to the HVAC systems by carefully considering building occupants’ thermal comfort profiles. Through the application of data-driven techniques and encompassing case studies from both industrial and residential buildings, this paper not only unveils pivotal opportunities for aggregators in the balancing and emerging flexibility markets but also successfully develops and demonstrates end-to-end practical tools for aggregators.

articleTitle: Evaluation of temporal light artefacts in tunable white solid state light sources
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: The Temporal Light Artefacts (TLAs) represent a significant concern in the field of lighting technology, impacting visual comfort and potentially causing health issues. Among the various metrics, the short-term flicker index (PstLM) has emerged as a robust indicator, reflecting the human eye's sensitivity to temporal variations in light intensity. Apart from the P stLM, the stroboscopic visibility measure (SVM) is another metric that was developed to assess the likelihood of stroboscopic effects, such as flicker or motion perception, in artificial lighting systems. This paper explores the evaluation of tunable white LED luminaires in terms of temporal light modulation. The evaluation concerns the measurement of both PstLM and SVM following the requirements of the recently introduced standards IEC TR 61547-1 and IEC TR 63158 as well as the EU Eco-design Regulation. The results are then compared with other LED lighting products as well as legacy light sources, i.e. incandescent and fluorescent lamps. Useful conclusions can be deduced from the measurements that can be used for the assessment of temporal light modulation in solid state light sources both conventional and tunable white.

articleTitle: Exploring a 2030 nearly 100% renewable Spanish electricity system from a capacity-mix adequacy perspective
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Nowadays, the increase in gas prices in Europe is fostering the penetration of renewable generation in electricity systems and pressing countries to accelerate the energy transition. It is then arguable whether goals on decarbonizing the system by 2030 set by National Energy and Climate Plans might be revisited towards more ambitious ones. This study explores the viability from a capacity-mix adequacy perspective of meeting a 2030 nearly 100% renewable Spanish electricity system without compromising the security of supply and economic affordability. The study builds scenarios with a progressively higher share of renewable energy production using a generation/storage expansion planning model. Renewable energy production shares, CO2 emissions, generation technologies, investment, and operation costs are monitored and discussed. The paper shows the viability of reaching renewable energy production shares as high as 95% at a reasonable cost and also how the cost significantly increases when trying to reach higher percentage values.

articleTitle: Solar power nowcasting using satellite images and deep learning advances
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: Accurate nowcasting of solar power production is crucial for power system operators and energy market participants. However, estimating real-time aggregated solar power production over a wide area is challenging due to spatial distribution, small-to- medium-range installations, and lack of smart metering facilities. This study investigates the application of deep neural architectures, such as U-Net, Vision Transformer, and Yolo, to extract cloud dynamic features from satellite imagery and estimate the aggregated solar power production of the Hellenic interconnected distribution system. The performance of these models is compared with a state-of-the-art solar power forecasting model that uses numerical weather predictions (NWPs) from the European Meteorological Service (ECMWF).

articleTitle: Permissioned blockchain-based monitoring framework for DER-integrated distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2024)
abstract: SCADA systems are used for real-time monitoring of key systems and the status of critical assets in both transmission and distribution networks. The trend towards different types of ”new” loads and sources such as photovoltaic (PV), electric vehicle (EV) charging stations and battery storage systems is changing the operational approach of distribution grids.
